landing.faq.ci.answer: Yes. An API key lets you trigger a scan from GitHub Actions, GitLab CI or any other pipeline, then read back the project's grade. Scheduled scans also run daily, weekly or monthly.
landing.faq.ci.question: Can I run a scan from my CI?
landing.faq.data_sources.answer: From public sources: OSV.dev for vulnerabilities, FIRST (EPSS score) for the likelihood of exploitation, the CISA catalog for vulnerabilities exploited in the wild, endoflife.date for runtimes and the official registries for versions.
landing.faq.data_sources.question: Where does the data come from?
landing.faq.false_positive.answer: An administrator can dismiss a vulnerability by stating why. It no longer counts toward the grade, and the justification stays on record.
landing.faq.false_positive.question: What about false positives?
landing.faq.private_repos.answer: Yes. Provide a GitHub or GitLab token for your organization: Sentinel only uses it to read. For an internal GitLab, enter your instance's address; it must present a certificate issued by a public authority, as internal certificate authorities are not supported.
landing.faq.private_repos.question: Are private repositories supported?
landing.faq.security.answer: Tokens are encrypted at rest and only used to read your repositories. Each organization is isolated at the database level, and every sensitive access is recorded in an audit log.
landing.faq.security.question: How are my tokens and data protected?
landing.faq.source_code.answer: No. Only manifests, lockfiles and runtime version files are read. Your code is neither analyzed nor stored.
landing.faq.source_code.question: Does Sentinel read my source code?
landing.faq.title: Frequently asked questions.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: Information for users about how their personal data is processed in Sentinel, in accordance with Article 13 of the GDPR.
privacy.roles.title: Data controller
privacy.roles.body: Sentinel is a personal, non-commercial project. The data controller is its publisher, who decides which projects are analyzed and who is invited to use the tool.
privacy.purposes.title: Purposes and legal bases
privacy.purposes.body: Each processing operation relies on a legal basis under Article 6 of the GDPR:
privacy.purposes.item.service: Monitoring the technical health and security of the analyzed projects (dependencies, score, tickets, exports): the publisher's legitimate interest.
privacy.purposes.item.account: Managing accounts and access, invitations, email verification, password reset: the publisher's legitimate interest.
privacy.purposes.item.security: Security, access logging and abuse prevention: the publisher's legitimate interest in protecting the tool.
privacy.purposes.item.no_profiling: No fully automated decision producing legal effects is made.
privacy.recipients.title: Recipients and processors
privacy.recipients.body: Data is accessible to the members of your organization in Sentinel and to the following providers, acting as processors:
privacy.recipients.item.hosting: Hosting: Vercel for the interface and Render for the API (technical logs including IP address), Supabase on Amazon Web Services infrastructure for the database.
privacy.recipients.item.email: Transactional emails: the SMTP provider configured by the publisher.
privacy.recipients.item.repos: Code hosts (GitHub, the configured GitLab instance), queried with the access token you provide, solely to read dependency manifests.
privacy.recipients.item.transfers: Some providers may process data outside the European Union. Such transfers are governed by the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
privacy.retention.title: Retention periods
privacy.retention.body: Data is retained for the following periods, then deleted or anonymised:
privacy.retention.account.label: User account
privacy.retention.account.value: For as long as the account exists, then deletion or pseudonymization of identifying data.
privacy.retention.activity.label: Activity and tickets
privacy.retention.activity.value: Retained in anonymised form after account deletion, to preserve the integrity of the organization's history.
privacy.retention.audit.label: Audit logs
privacy.retention.audit.value: 12 months from the event, in line with CNIL recommendations.
privacy.retention.tokens.label: Revoked tokens
privacy.retention.tokens.value: Until their expiry date, then automatically purged.
privacy.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.rights.body: You have the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability, as well as the right to issue directives on the fate of your data after your death.
privacy.rights.item.self_service: Access, rectification, data export and account deletion can be carried out directly from your profile.
privacy.rights.item.request: Other requests go to your organization's administrator or to the publisher; you will receive an answer within one month.
privacy.rights.item.complaint: You may lodge a complaint with the CNIL, 3 place de Fontenoy, 75007 Paris — www.cnil.fr.
privacy.rights.profile_link: Manage my data from my profile
privacy.contact.title: Contact
privacy.contact.body: For any question about data protection or to exercise your rights, contact your organization's administrator or the publisher of Sentinel.
